title: Redwood All-Hands - August 2026
summary: Monthly company all-hands covering Q2 results, product updates (Dedicated, Private), runtime/benchmark highlights, security posture (SOC2 roadmap), hiring and org changes, and OKRs. Leadership recapped wins, noted areas to accelerate (cost optimization, observability adoption), and set clear next steps for product docs and customer outreach.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (CEO): Hey everyone, welcome to the August all-hands. Appreciate folks joining especially folks dialing in from APAC, thanks for staying late. We're about 60 minutes, we'll do leadership updates then Q&A.

[00:28] Lucas (CTO): Quick infra note — thanks to the infra team we dropped P95 latency by ~12% on the hosted API after the kernel selection change; that's on the models with long context. There's still some tail issues on multi-region routing, working on a fix.

[01:05] Priya (VP Eng): Yeah, the kernel selector rollback earlier this month cost us a few hours, but the 1.2.3 rollout yesterday looks stable. We saw a small regression with KV cache warmup in canaries, so we tuned the batching thresholds.

[01:45] Audience (Employee 1): is that the KV as K-V? sometimes the transcript swaps that, will docs show the change?

[01:52] Priya: yes, KV cache - we'll update the rollout notes in Confluence and the runbook. Expect the doc link in the summary email.

[02:20] Ethan (Head of Product): On product — Dedicated GA extension is on track for Sept 30th, Private deployment lab testing is going good but we pushed out the on-prem packaging for a couple of key integrations (KMS/HSM support) to mid-October. We prioritized customer security integrations based on feedback from our early pilots.

[03:00] Jordan (Head of Revenue): From GTM — churn is down 1.8% quarter-over-quarter for customers on Dedicated; expansion motions are healthy. Top asks from customers: clearer cost model, predictable latency SLOs, and more observability dashboards out of the box.

[03:35] Maya: Thanks. Quick finance highlight — we beat our Q2 revenue plan by about 6%. Burn is slightly higher than expected because of spot market GPU purchases during the trial bursts. We'll tighten capital allocation next quarter.

[04:05] Lucas: Benchmarks — short story: we published the benchmark sheet to the public repo; it's labeled as 'prelim' because there are measurement inconsistencies across regions. The team is reconciling perf counters and will re-run the full suite by end of next week.

[04:45] Audience (Employee 2): are we showing comparisons vs openai and anthro- —

[04:50] Lucas: we mention OpenAI and Anthropic generally in the competitive deck but focus on infra and economics; don't leak any customer-specific numbers.

[05:12] Priya: Security — SAML/SSO improvements are shipping this week. SOC 2 readiness: controls mostly in place, control owner list is up on the security confluence page. Audit window targeted for Q4.

[05:35] Maya: Hiring & org changes: we promoted Priya to VP Eng, congrats again; we're also hiring for two senior infra SWE roles and a product marketing lead. Hiring priority list is in the hiring doc.

[06:05] Priya: small note — reorg on infra: we merged the batching team and the runtime team to reduce handoffs; should speed up kernel/selector iteration cycles.

[06:30] Ethan: Roadmap highlights: Q3 focus is on latency SLO tooling (per-route SLAs), caching improvements (prefix cache), and Redwood Optimize launches for pilot customers. We'll open a limited beta for Optimize in September.

[07:05] Employee question (anonymous via chat): any update on pricing?

[07:12] Jordan: Pricing work is ongoing; the goal is to publish clearer unit economics - per-token, per-embedding, and also bundle options for Dedicated. Expect a draft to the sales team next week.

[07:40] Audience crosstalk / filler: mm-hmm, okay, cool.

[08:00] Lucas: A technical deep-dive coming next Tuesday for folks interested — 45 minutes on kernel selection, batching and inference cache; sign up link in the staff slack.

[08:20] Maya: Customer wins: shout-out to three customers who went live on Dedicated this quarter — names redacted for privacy but big wins for ARR. Team ramped quickly on private deploy checks.

[09:00] Priya: Ops highlight: mean time to repair for critical incidents is down 20% QoQ thanks to the new runbook templates and playbooks. Thanks to on-call folks for the extra hours.

[09:30] Employee 3: small question about observability - are we standardizing dashboards?

[09:38] Ethan: Yes, the console will ship templated dashboards for per-route latency/cost; early customers will get a custom view. We need Product-Eng to lock the schema by end of week.

[10:05] Maya: OKRs quick callout — company top-level OKRs: 1) Improve inference cost by 18% across hosted traffic, 2) Achieve SOC 2 audit readiness and start the audit, 3) Launch Redwood Optimize beta, 4) Reduce multi-region tail latency by 15%. We'll break these down in team syncs.

[10:45] Audience (Employee 4): is there a playbook for selling Optimize?

[10:50] Jordan: Yes, sales enablement is building a pitch deck and ROI calculator — expect draft next Tue.

[11:10] Lucas: A brief technical caveat — some of the latency improvements rely on a new quantization path that isn't GA yet; we'll flag models that shouldn't be auto-quantized until we've validated output quality.

[11:40] Priya: On quality monitoring — we launched a regression alerts prototype tied to prompt sets. We need engineering to add more canaries to avoid noisy alerts.

[12:05] Employee 5: question about Private deployment pricing and support SLAs?

[12:12] Jordan: Private pricing will be contractual — platform fee + support tier, with Reserved capacity as an add-on. We are aligning legal and finance to produce a template.

[12:38] Maya: Partnerships update — we signed a channel partner in EMEA to help with regulated customers; not huge yet but a good beachhead.

[13:00] Audience side comments / short clarifications.

[13:20] Maya: Alright we'll open up for Q&A — please keep questions short, we have about 45 minutes of discussion left.

[13:40] Employee 6: what's the plan for community & OSS engagement this quarter?

[13:46] Ethan: We'll sponsor two conferences and release a reference app for private deployments (lightweight helm charts) — not full on OSS but helpful for partners.

[14:15] Employee 7: are we still pulling model catalog from the same source? I saw a mismatch in the verify profiles.

[14:22] Lucas: Good catch — there's a sync bug between the catalog metadata service and the performance profiling pipeline. Team has a fix, expect a patch tomorrow.

[14:50] Employee 8: any thoughts on adding more region coverage APAC?

[14:55] Maya: We are expanding regions based on demand and partner support; capacity planning team will post the tentative schedule for additional APAC zones.

[15:25] Priya: One more note — please make sure any runbooks changed during incident drills have a brief changelog entry. It helps audits and onboarding.

[15:40] Maya: Closing notes: big thanks to everyone — wins and hard work are visible. We will circulate the recording, the slides, and a one-pager with action items.

[16:00] Ethan: Reminder — leadership office hours after this for product questions.

[16:10] Maya: Ok that's it, thanks folks, end of all-hands.

[16:20] (Recording ends)

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker label noise typical of automatic meeting transcripts; timestamps are approximate and used for navigation.
action_items: Priya Singh: Share revised infra cost model and rollout notes by 2026-08-27
Ethan Brooks: Publish product rollout timeline and GA dates for Dedicated & Private by 2026-08-24
Jordan Lee: Send draft pricing/ROI calculator to sales team by 2026-08-26
Security team: Upload SOC2 attestation checklist and control owner list to Confluence by 2026-08-31
next_steps: Leadership to circulate slides + recording within 24 hours
Engineering to re-run benchmark suite and publish updated sheet by 2026-08-27
Recruiting to post new infra SWE roles and PMM role by end of the week
